record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: For every cubic planar graph G and every 3-list-assignment L of G, is it always possible to choose two pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings, meaning two proper colorings from the same lists that assign different colors to each vertex?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3 Is it possible to choose two disjoint proper colourings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a cubic planar graph, i.e., a planar graph in which every vertex has degree exactly $3$. A list-assignment $L$ on $G$ assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ a set $L(v)$ of admissible colors, and is called a $3$-list-assignment if $|L(v)|=3$ for every $v\in V$. A proper $L$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c:V\to\bigcup_{v\in V}L(v)$ such that $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v\in V$ and $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $uv\in E$. Two proper $L$-colorings $c_1$ and $c_2$ are said to be disjoint if $c_1(v)\neq c_2(v)$ for every $v\in V$.

Decide whether the following statement is true: for every cubic planar graph $G$ and every $3$-list-assignment $L$ on $G$, there exist two disjoint proper $L$-colorings of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on disjoint list-colorings of planar graphs (Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Zhu, 2023) establishes that two disjoint L-colorings exist for planar graphs of girth at least 8, but does not resolve the cubic planar case with 3-lists. No source found confirming a resolution of the specific cubic planar question, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Two disjoint L-colorings are guaranteed if the girth is at least 8; a fractional packing exists when the girth is at least 6.
status_evidence.claim: Known results on disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs require girth conditions and do not settle the cubic planar case.

status_evidence.title: Packing list-colorings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence of k pairwise-disjoint proper colorings from k-list-assignments.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational paper on list packing; cubic planar 3-list case not resolved here.
